summary: Kingfisher Health: sustained streaming oscillation causing degraded conversational throughput — customer escalation and restoration plan
description:
Issue summary:
Between 2026-03-02 03:10 UTC and 2026-03-02 07:40 UTC Kingfisher Health experienced a sustained oscillation in streaming response progress for conversational requests. Symptoms included long tail token latencies (500ms -> 6s spikes), occasional partial transcripts, and client-observed reconnects. Impact: production user-facing degradation for two mission-critical endpoints (session-chats v2 and claims-parser).

Impact:
- ~18% increase in 95/99 token-latency for the affected routes in us-east.
- Multiple streamed responses truncated or repeated by client due to reconnects, causing downstream deduplication and billing noise.
- Kingfisher reported several enterprise SLA breaches and opened an escalation call at 05:00 UTC.

Environment:
- Redwood Hosted API (prod), region: us-east-1
- Customer on enterprise plan with pinned model gpt-open-20b:quantized-v2
- Deployment used streaming websocket connections with prefix caching enabled

Timeline and steps to reproduce observed by Support:
1) 03:08 UTC — surge in request rate from Kingfisher identified by our APM; tail latencies begin rising.
2) 03:12 UTC — first customer report via support chat; session IDs and sample traces attached.
3) 03:20–04:00 UTC — repeated streaming disconnects and partial transcripts observed; autoscaler triggered several times.
4) 04:10 UTC — SRE engaged; hypothesis: autoscaler thrash + KV-prefix cache invalidation under high multiplexing.
5) 05:00 UTC — customer escalation call; agreed immediate mitigation: temporarily disable multiplexed affinity and pin to dedicated serving pool.

Logs / Observations:
- Frontend gateway logs show 502/524 spikes correlated with backend queue depth rising.
- Serving-runtime metrics: per-instance token-walltime increased, sustained small GC stalls on quantized kernel paths.
- Autoscaler logs: scale-up/scale-down loop within 1-2 minute intervals for the affected pool.
- KV cache misses spiked for sessions with high fanout.

Additional context:
Kingfisher routes exhibit high multiplexing: single logical session fanouts across 6 parallel streams. This increased pressure on KV prefix cache coordination and occasionally triggered request replays when a worker dropped mid-response.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: autoscaler oscillation in combination with small GC stalls on quantized kernels produced transient backpressure that manifested as streaming stalls and client reconnects.
Observed autoscaler policy: aggressive cool-down set to 60s with threshold at 60% cpu/util. Under bursty traffic this oscillated due to request-per-second variance across instances.
Quantized kernel path flagged: longer-than-expected token-generation jitter when GPU memory pressure + small host GC occurred. Observed on fractional-quantized variants (quantized-v2).

KV cache coordination: cache invalidations during worker churn led to temporary missing prefixes, causing fallback replay behavior in the serving runtime (we replay partial tokens when prefix unavailable).

SRE reproduced localized oscillation in staging by replaying Kingfisher request pattern with 6x multiplexing and short autoscaler cool-down; reproduced the scale-up/scale-down loop and increased partial transcripts.
mitigation_steps: Immediate: removed multiplex affinity (fanout=1) for Kingfisher sessions at 05:05 UTC — visible latency normalized within ~6 minutes.
Hotfix: pin Kingfisher to dedicated serving pool (reserved instances) to avoid autoscaler churn — applied 05:25 UTC.
Customer accommodation: issued pro-rata credit for impacted time window and committed to a technical postmortem and follow-up call.
resolution: Root cause determined to be combination of autoscaler oscillation (too-low cool-down) and sensitivity in quantized kernel path under high fanout. Permanent fixes: increased autoscaler cool-down and added a short warm-up buffer for dedicated pools; improved fallback-only replay logic to avoid duplicate partial transcripts. Deployed configuration changes 2026-03-03 02:30 UTC. Customer confirmed restoration and acceptable performance on 2026-03-03 04:00 UTC.
